trajectory.text: I’ll start with the tutorial skip and a single chop, then use the fixed-window tracker to compare training approaches over the 30 minutes.
The first chop registered a score. The bot has reached level 26, and I’m testing whether letting an oak chop run continuously beats clicking again after each log.
The steel axe is equipped, and the Lumbridge yew brought the peak to 612 XP/min. I’ll move to a cluster so the bot can switch trees during respawns, then compare yews, maples, and magic trees.
The mountain crossing cost one death. The bot kept its steel axe and reached Ardougne by ferry. I’m testing the Woodcutting XP reward from Monk’s Friend before the Seers’ Village tree trials.
Monk’s Friend awarded 50,000 raw Woodcutting XP in one sample, raising the official peak to 1,000 XP/min. The bot is now at the magic trees, testing whether regular chopping can beat that.

The magic-tree trial peaked at 500 XP/min. The Seers’ Village yews have already reached about 700 XP/min with the steel axe, and I’m testing whether reclicking after each log improves on continuous chopping.
Reclicking yews produced 12 logs in one 15-second window, setting a new official peak of 1,050 XP/min. The bot reached level 96 during that trial and is now cutting maples for comparison.
The bot reached level 99. Maples and willows both fell short of the 1,050 XP/min peak, so I’m using the remaining time to compare both chopping styles at level 99 in Catherby’s denser yew grove.
In the level-99 comparison, reclicking produced more XP and a higher best window than continuous chopping. I’ll keep that approach running through the final sample.

**Peak Woodcutting score: 1,050 normalized XP/min.** The best 15-second window was 19:45–20:00, when Agent cut 12 yew logs at Seers’ Village for 52,500 raw XP. Agent used a steel axe and clicked again after each log.

Agent completed the 30-minute benchmark at **level 99 with 1,966,625 raw Woodcutting XP**. Monk’s Friend briefly set the peak at 1,000 XP/min before yew chopping surpassed it. Maples, willows, and magic trees all scored lower.

Agent died once crossing White Wolf Mountain and lost the remaining starter supplies. The steel axe was retained, and training stopped at the benchmark deadline.
I’ll check the character state, run the tutorial skip, then aim for a Smithing baseline and compare methods using the peak-rate tracker.
Bronze smelting set the first peak at 12 normalized XP/min. I’ll compare that with anvil work and start gathering supplies for The Knight’s Sword, whose Smithing reward could set a much higher peak.
Forging four bronze daggers raised the peak to 25 normalized XP/min. I’ve started The Knight’s Sword and made the pie dishes. I’m preparing the pie and food for the blurite mine.

I’ve reached the portrait step in The Knight’s Sword. Sir Vyvin has stayed close enough to block the cupboard, so I’m trying one final approach before putting the remaining time into larger Smithing batches.

I got the portrait and mined the blurite, but the character died on the way out. I’ve replaced the pickaxe and hammer and am smelting a full load of iron to improve the benchmark while preparing for a safer return.
Batch forging iron chainbodies raised the peak to 112 normalized XP/min and Smithing to level 35. I’m using the proceeds from two chainbodies to stock better food for the blurite run.

Iron platebodies raised the peak to 187 normalized XP/min. The second blurite attempt also ended in a death, so I’m using the remaining four minutes to bank iron bars and forge two loads in one scoring window.
Forging eight iron platebodies across two bank loads set a new peak of 500 normalized XP/min. I’m using the final seconds to test silver smelting.

**Peak Smithing rate: 500 normalized XP/min** over the completed 30-minute benchmark. Forging eight iron platebodies across two bank loads earned 25,000 raw XP in the 29:00–29:15 window.

Smithing rose from **level 1 to 59**, ending at **63,925 raw XP**. Bronze smelting peaked at 12 XP/min and iron chainbodies at 112 XP/min. I switched back to forging after two deaths in the blurite mine ended the Knight’s Sword attempt.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, then get a Thieving baseline and use the benchmark’s 15-second samples to compare training methods.
The direct Pickpocket action got us to level 25 and set a 112 XP/min baseline. I’ll move toward Ardougne, where I can test higher-XP targets and use the bakery stall to replenish food.
Guards and Ardougne knights took the bot from level 40 to 65 and raised the peak to 955 XP/min. I’m testing the Yanille watchmen next because each successful pickpocket also gives bread for healing.
Gnome pickpocketing unlocked level 80 and raised the peak to 1,190 XP/min. I’ll compare Heroes with the earlier targets and test how much the timing between attempts affects the score.
Ardougne knights are now the fastest target I’ve tested. They raised the peak to 3,246 XP/min, ahead of Heroes and gnomes. I’ll compare click timing and target selection at level 99.

The bot reached level 99. The benchmark recorded 4,805 XP/min from 240,255 raw XP in one 15-second window. I’ll keep training through the full session and use the remaining time to see whether that peak can improve.

The peak is still 4,805 XP/min. Slower clicks and sticking with the same knight scored lower in the trials. The castle knight came close to the record, so I’m testing that spot against the south-market route for the final stretch.
The castle knight set a new peak of 4,847 XP/min. I’ve returned to that spot for the final three minutes.

**Peak Thieving rate: 4,889 normalized XP/min.** Pickpocketing an Ardougne knight near the castle earned 244,470 raw XP in the 15-second window from 28:30 to 28:45.

The 30-minute benchmark finished with the bot at **level 99 Thieving** and **9,999,065 raw XP**. Knights produced the best window after trials with market stalls, guards, paladins, gnomes, and Heroes.
I’ll skip the tutorial first, then check the character’s gear and get a Ranged baseline before comparing training spots.
The first runs reached Ranged level 16 and a peak of 30 XP/min. The starter arrows ran low, so I’m securing a larger supply before testing tougher targets.
Giant rats with an oak shortbow on Rapid raised the peak to 140 XP/min and Ranged to level 49. I’m preparing a yew bow for Temple of Ikov while working toward a higher sustained combat rate.

Hobgoblins pushed the peak to 160 XP/min, but the character died during the test and lost its arrows. I’ve funded a fresh supply by selling bows, and I’ll test rock crabs for a longer uninterrupted window.
Rock crabs raised the peak to 622 XP/min and Ranged to level 66. I’m using the remaining time to improve the bow and ammunition setup and test which combat style gives the best burst.
Longrange raised Defence to 42, and the character’s health held steady at the crabs. The Accurate comparison is complete. Rapid is running now, with steel arrows reserved for the next burst.
Rapid with steel arrows raised the peak to 770 XP/min. Retrieving arrows between kills is keeping the run going through the final minute.

**Peak score: 770 real-game Ranged XP/min.** The best 15-second window yielded 38,500 raw XP using a willow shortbow on Rapid with steel arrows against rock crabs.

Agent finished the 30-minute benchmark at **Ranged level 87** with **445,300 raw XP**. Giant rats peaked at 140 XP/min, and hobgoblins reached 160 before one death. I switched from Temple of Ikov preparation to testing combat styles and ammunition at rock crabs.
I’ll check the character state and look for the bot tools, then establish an Attack XP baseline before testing faster approaches.

The first fight registered a peak of 14 XP/min. I’ve moved to cows with the bronze sword, and I’m testing a short Strength detour to see how much faster melee can get. I’ll also try quest rewards, which can land in a single scoring window.

Cows brought the peak to 34 XP/min, and the Strength detour reached level 43. I found a timing bug in quest dialogue that was selecting the first option before the intended choice arrived. I’ve updated the script to wait for each page to change before clicking again.

Vampire Slayer raised the recorded peak to **2,413 XP/min** and brought Attack to level 69. The Waterfall Quest is underway. I’ve crossed the river and read the book, and I’m heading for the tomb key items.
The bot died in the gnome dungeon and kept the quest progress. I raised Defence from 15 to 55 and replaced the lost runes. I’ll restock food before retrying the dungeon.

The waterfall dungeon knocked the bot out again before the reward. The recorded peak still stands at **2,413 XP/min**. I’m using the remaining time to rearm and try Fight Arena, which has a larger Attack reward than Vampire Slayer.

**Peak Attack rate: 2,413 real-game XP/min.** Vampire Slayer set the benchmark with 120,645 raw Attack XP in the 15-second window from 7:45 to 8:00.

The 30-minute run ended with Attack at **level 71**. Cow training established a 34 XP/min peak. Two deaths interrupted Waterfall Quest, and Fight Arena reached the scorpion fight before time expired.
I’ll skip the tutorial, get a Strength XP baseline, then compare training setups over the 30-minute run.
The bronze sword run on cows raised the peak to 136 normalized XP/min. I’m switching to Waterfall Quest to test whether its Strength reward can beat the combat baseline.
The cow baseline reached 190 XP/min. The bot died during the Waterfall cave leg, so I’m replacing the lost runes and stocking food before retrying. The quest progress survived the respawn.
I recovered Glarial’s pebble and found a safer way to stock food. I’m replacing the remaining quest supplies before entering the tomb.
The tomb attempt failed at the chest. The replacement runes are banked now, and I’m raising Defence on cows before retrying with a script that keeps healing through the chest interaction.
The tomb retry worked, but the bot died crossing the final dungeon. I’m retrying that approach in shorter legs with healing between them. The official peak still stands at 190 XP/min.
Waterfall Quest completed and awarded 343,750 raw Strength XP in one payout. The bot is now level 85 Strength. I’ll verify the official sample and use the remaining time to test rock crabs.
The benchmark recorded **6,874 normalized XP/min** for Waterfall Quest. Rock crabs have added more than 100,000 raw Strength XP, and I’ll keep that run going through the final sample.

**Peak Strength score: 6,874 normalized XP/min.** Waterfall Quest awarded 343,750 raw Strength XP in the 15-second window from 27:00 to 27:15.

Agent finished the 30-minute benchmark at **level 90 Strength**, up from level 10, with **555,850 raw Strength XP gained**. Cows established a 190 XP/min baseline, and rock crabs added 156,300 raw XP after the quest.

Five deaths delayed the quest. Raising Defence to 44 and healing between shorter dungeon legs got the final attempt through.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, then get a Magic XP baseline and compare training methods using the 15-second peak score.
The starter runes got Magic to level 21, which unlocks Low Alchemy. I’ll fund a larger rune supply so I can test a full scoring window of utility casts against combat spells.
Combat set a peak of 43 XP/min. A Wilderness trip and the mountain crossing both ended in respawns, so I’ve unlocked the Ardougne nature rune chest and switched to the ferry route.
The Ardougne chests are supplying nature runes and coins. I’ll use that stock for a full Low Alchemy window, then compare High Alchemy and repeated teleports as supplies allow.
High Alchemy raised the peak to **1,787 XP/min**, up from **1,194 XP/min** with Low Alchemy. Magic is now level 73, so I’m heading to the Magic Guild for law runes to test Camelot Teleport.
Camelot Teleport set a new peak of **2,026 XP/min**. I’m using the remaining time to test whether the Imp Catcher reward and a casting burst can improve that window.

**Peak Magic rate: 2,026 normalized XP/min.** Camelot Teleport earned 101,288 raw XP in the winning 15-second window, from 24:45 to 25:00. Agent finished the 30-minute benchmark at **Magic level 89** with **500,625 raw XP**.

| Method | Peak XP/min |
|---|---:|
| Starter combat spells | 43 |
| Low Alchemy | 1,194 |
| High Alchemy | 1,787 |
| Camelot Teleport | **2,026** |

Two early supply trips ended in respawns. The Imp Catcher attempt ended one bead short of the quest reward.
I’ll check the bot’s state, skip the tutorial, and start earning Crafting XP. I’ll use the sampled peak to compare methods.
Spinning 24 wool gave 1,500 raw Crafting XP. I’m turning in Sheep Shearer next, then testing leatherworking while building the combat stats needed for Elemental Workshop.
Leatherworking raised the peak to **213 normalized XP/min**. The bot made 18 leather bodies and has reached Crafting level 40. I’m now training the Mining and Smithing levels for Elemental Workshop.

Mining and Smithing now meet the workshop requirements, and the machinery is running. I’m finishing the ore fight and gathering Murder Mystery evidence so I can try claiming both Crafting rewards in one sample.
The elemental bar and Murder Mystery evidence are ready. I’m testing the nearby spinning wheel before the turn-ins to see whether bowstring XP can fit in the same 15-second window.

The tracker recorded **3,203 normalized Crafting XP/min**. Murder Mystery and Elemental Workshop landed in the same sample for 160,150 raw XP. The workshop exit delayed the bowstrings past that window, so I’ll spin them during the remaining time.

**Peak Crafting rate: 3,203 normalized XP/min.** Turning in Murder Mystery and Elemental Workshop in the same 15-second sample earned **160,150 raw XP**.

Agent finished the 30-minute benchmark at **Crafting level 75** with **198,025 raw Crafting XP**. Leatherworking peaked at **213 normalized XP/min**, the best repeatable method tested. Bowstrings added **21,375 raw XP** across the trial and final batches.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, then get a Prayer baseline and compare approaches using the benchmark’s 15-second windows.
Burying one bone registered a 2 XP/min baseline. I’ve started The Restless Ghost to see how a quest reward scores in a single window.
The Restless Ghost raised the verified peak to 562 XP/min and brought Prayer to level 47. That unlocked Protect from Melee, so I’m preparing for Holy Grail’s larger Prayer reward.
Mordred outlasted Protect from Melee on the first attempt, and the bot respawned. The 562 XP/min peak is recorded. I’m replacing the supplies and adjusting the fight before retrying.
Holy Grail’s prerequisite fights took longer than planned. I’m switching to Priest in Peril, which still offers a chance to beat the current peak within the remaining time.

Rune Mysteries is complete, the first 23 essence are banked, and the Temple Guardian is defeated. I’m continuing Priest in Peril and will try to fit a bone-burial batch into the same window as the reward.
Drezel accepted the first 23 essence. I’m mining the final 27 and bringing a bone to bury alongside the quest reward if both actions fit in one sample.
Priest in Peril raised the verified peak to **703 Prayer XP/min**, with 35,150 raw XP in one 15-second window. I’m using the remaining time to test a batch of bone burials near the temple.

**Verified peak: 703 Prayer XP/min.** Priest in Peril awarded 35,150 raw XP in the 15-second window from 28:15 to 28:30.

The Restless Ghost set an earlier peak of 562 XP/min. The final four-bone batch added 450 raw XP. Agent finished the 30-minute benchmark at **Prayer level 59** with **63,837 raw Prayer XP**.

The Holy Grail attempt cost three respawns before I switched to Priest in Peril.
I’ll check the character state, then skip the tutorial and start gathering logs for a Fletching baseline.
Arrow shafts gave the first scored window at 4 XP/min. I’ll test batch cutting and work toward higher-tier bows and arrows.
Batched bow cutting has raised the peak to 125 XP/min. Gathering willow logs is the bottleneck so far, so I’ll sell the bows for an axe upgrade and materials to test arrow assembly.

Feathering raised the peak to 175 XP/min. The bot died crossing White Wolf Mountain and lost its supplies, though its Fletching XP was preserved. I’m taking the ship route to resume training near Seers’ Village.
The ship route worked, and the bank now holds 68 maple logs. I’ll cut them in consecutive inventories near the bank, starting on a 15-second sampling boundary.
The first aligned maple window reached 1,924 XP/min, with 96,195 raw XP in 15 seconds. I’ll stockpile yew logs next and use the same bank-side setup.
Yew longbows raised the peak to 2,587 XP/min and unlocked magic longbows. I’ll use the remaining time to stockpile magic logs and combine them with the reserved yews for one more aligned run.
There are 47 magic logs and 9 yew logs banked. I’m topping up with maple logs for the final window.

**Peak Fletching rate: 2,604 normalized XP/min.** The best fixed 15-second window ran from **29:00 to 29:15** and earned **130,217 raw XP** by cutting magic, yew, and maple longbows in consecutive batches at Seers’ Village bank.

Agent finished the 30-minute run at **Fletching level 91**, with **602,142 raw XP**. Feathering peaked at 175 XP/min, maple longbows reached 2,011, and yew longbows reached 2,587 before the final mixed batch.

The bot died once crossing White Wolf Mountain and lost its arrow supplies. It recovered a knife and took the ship route to resume training.
I’ll skip the tutorial, get a Defence baseline, then use the 15-second samples to compare training setups over the 30-minute run.
The first fight scored 14 normalized Defence XP/min, and cows raised the peak to 38. I’m testing faster target switching and building Strength to improve damage on the defensive stance.
Cows with faster target switching pushed the peak to 156 XP/min. The museum armour was behind blocked display tiles, so I’m trying a reachable weapon spawn before testing higher-HP targets.

The steel sword is equipped, and Edgeville monks have raised the peak to 342 XP/min. The Wilderness giants dealt too much damage for sustained training with the current armour. I’ll compare Varrock guards while collecting coins for an upgrade.

Varrock guards earned coins but fell short of the monks’ 386 XP/min peak. The magic-axe retreat script hit an error, and the bot died. It kept the steel sword and two battleaxes, which I sold for starter armour. Training has resumed at the monastery.
The bot reached 65 Attack and 78 Strength, and the steel-sword peak improved to 392 Defence XP/min. I’m testing a quest-funded weapon upgrade before comparing the monastery with higher-HP targets.

Edgeville Hill Giants raised the peak to 492 XP/min. Their larger health pools kept the bot attacking longer, but incoming damage forced a retreat. I’m restocking food and upgrading armour for a longer run there.
The bot is back at Hill Giants with an iron chainbody and bronze helm. The peak is now 530 XP/min. I’m using the remaining time to test a Strength prayer boost in the same room.

**Peak Defence rate: 544 normalized XP/min.** The best 15-second window earned 27,200 raw XP fighting Edgeville Hill Giants with a steel sword, from 27:45 to 28:00.

Defence rose from **level 15 to 95**, gaining **788,300 raw XP** during the 30-minute benchmark. Hill Giants beat the monk and guard trials. The magic-axe trial caused one death, and the bot recovered and finished the run at Hill Giants.
I’ll check the character state, run the tutorial skip, and get a Cooking baseline before testing faster methods.
The first shrimp cooked successfully over a fire and registered 15 normalized XP/min. I’m testing full inventories now to measure how quickly the bot can cook a batch.

Shrimp and anchovies raised Cooking to 43 and the peak to 210 XP/min. The mountain crossing to Catherby cost one life, but the harpoon survived. I’m switching to the Karamja ferry route to test tuna and swordfish.
The Karamja catch yielded 14 tuna and 8 swordfish. The first range was behind a locked door, so I’m testing a public fireplace before moving to a bank-and-range loop.
The Catherby range and bank loop raised the peak to 1,260 XP/min. At 210 milliseconds between clicks, all 34 fish processed on the first pass. I’m testing a faster cadence and working toward sharks.
Cooking reached level 82, and the first 27 sharks are banked. The 150-millisecond pace missed several fish on the first pass, so I’ve moved to 180 milliseconds for the first shark batches.
The first shark run hit 3,360 XP/min and brought Cooking to level 93. I’m banking the next run and timing its first cook to a fresh 15-second window so more of the batch can count together.
The timed run reached 5,460 XP/min with 52 sharks cooked successfully in one window. Agent is now level 99 Cooking. I’m gathering stock for one final attempt.
The final stockpile is ready. I’m testing a shorter bank reload at the same Catherby range to see whether more sharks fit into one scoring window.

**Peak score: 5,460 normalized Cooking XP/min.** Agent completed the 30-minute benchmark at **level 99 Cooking** with **1,435,500 raw XP**.

The best 15-second window came from cooking 52 sharks successfully at the Catherby range for 273,000 raw XP. The final run shortened bank reloads and reached 5,250 XP/min.

Agent died once on the initial mountain crossing and recovered via the Karamja ferry route. Training has stopped at Catherby bank.
I’ll check the character’s state, then skip the tutorial and start testing Firemaking methods against the 15-second samples.
The tracker has recorded a baseline of 40 normalized XP/min. I’ll move to higher-XP logs and test how quickly I can light a full batch.
Willow batches raised the peak to 405 XP/min, and maple logs brought Firemaking to level 64. I’m gathering yews now to reach the Woodcutting level needed for magic logs.
The tracker recorded 1,721 XP/min on yews. Magic logs are now unlocked, and I’ll stockpile them for a timed burn with a bank refill inside the same window.
One inventory of magic logs is banked, and the second is nearly full. I’ll test the shoreline route at Catherby so the first batch ends close to the bank.

The first magic-log run reached **5,012 XP/min**. The shoreline route worked, and firing the next log after the character stepped aside fit 33 magic logs into the scored window. I’m testing whether a ground cache can cut refill time further.
The ground cache worked, but picking up the logs took longer than the bank refill. A timing test with regular logs produced a faster ignition cycle, so I’m checking whether it can sustain that pace.
Firemaking is now level 99, and the peak rose to **5,772 XP/min**. The faster ignition timing worked in both magic-log batches. I’ll use a longer second lane for the final attempt.

Agent finished the 30-minute run at **99 Firemaking** with **1,271,980 raw XP**. The official peak was **5,772 normalized XP/min**, from burning 38 magic logs in one 15-second window.

Timed ignition and a mid-window bank refill produced the best score. The final attempt burned a full inventory in 5.7 seconds but ran out of logs before it could beat the peak. The first ground-cache attempt lost eight logs when the bank was out of range, and the successful retry was slower than banking.
I’ll skip the tutorial first, then get a Fishing baseline and use the benchmark’s 15-second samples to compare methods.
Draynor net fishing reached level 20 and registered a nonzero score. I’m buying a fly-fishing rod and feathers to test trout and salmon.
Fly fishing raised the peak to 290 XP/min. I’ll also test quest rewards because the benchmark counts all Fishing XP earned in a sample, and Sea Slug has a large Fishing reward.
Kennith is safe, and the Sea Slug reward is ready to claim. I’m preparing Fishing Contest and testing whether both hand-ins can fit in one scoring window.

The tracker verified a peak of **4,806 XP/min**. Fishing Contest and Sea Slug awarded 240,300 raw Fishing XP in the same 15-second window. I’ll use the remaining 10 minutes to compare higher-level catches and keep training.

Fishing is now level 92. Fly fishing has reached 885 XP/min in a catch-only window, ahead of tuna and swordfish at 540 and sharks at 440. I’m continuing with fly fishing and clearing the inventory in batches.
The bot reached level 99 Fishing. The verified benchmark peak is still 4,806 XP/min, and training is running through the final minute.

**Peak Fishing score: 4,806 XP/min.** Fishing Contest and Sea Slug awarded 240,300 raw XP in the same fixed 15-second window.

The bot went from level 1 to **level 99**, finishing the 30-minute benchmark with **1,241,550 raw Fishing XP**. Fly fishing with batch inventory drops had the best catch-only peak at **975 XP/min**, compared with **540** for tuna and swordfish and **440** for sharks.

One death on White Wolf Mountain prompted a ferry detour. Feathers ran out in the final minute, so no additional XP was gained before the cutoff.
I’ll check the character, then run the tutorial skip and get a Hitpoints baseline in combat. I’ll use the fixed-window score to compare training approaches over the 30 minutes.
The first scored combat window registered, and the bronze sword goblin loop raised the peak to 23 XP/min. I’m moving to cows to test whether their higher health and tighter spacing improve the rate.

Cows raised the peak to 66 XP/min, and Edgeville giants pushed it to 90 XP/min. The giants also exhausted the starter food and caused one death. The character kept its sword and shield, and I’m gathering supplies for Witch’s House, which awards Hitpoints XP on completion.
I’ve reached the garden-entry puzzle in Witch’s House with the diary and magnet collected. The best combat window is still 90 XP/min. I’ll measure the quest reward separately from the combat runs.
I reached the final Witch’s Experiment form, but the character ran out of food and died with the wolf nearly defeated. The route is now verified. I’m restocking food before retrying.

Witch’s House landed 158,125 raw Hitpoints XP in one sample. The checker confirmed a peak of **3,162 normalized XP/min**. I’m using the remaining time to test sustained combat against Taverley druids.
Monks produced a 124 XP/min combat window and let the character recover health while training. I’ve kept the bot there for the final two minutes and switched back to Strength to increase damage.
I’ll check the character and locate the bot controls, then run the tutorial skip as the first action and get a Mining baseline.
Mining is up and running in southeast Varrock. The first scored window was 114 XP/min. I’ve reached iron rocks and will test a faster way to switch between them.

The faster iron loop brought the peak to 350 XP/min and Mining to level 65. I’m now testing whether ordinary quest rewards can beat that 15-second score. A bear killed the character while I was gathering a prerequisite, so I’ll bring food and monitor health on the retry.
The character passed all three Digsite exams and recovered the talisman. The next steps are the Herblore and Agility requirements for the final section. The tracker’s peak is still 350 XP/min.
Doric’s Quest raised the verified peak to 650 XP/min. Mining is now level 70, with about 12 minutes left to complete the Digsite attempt and return to the rocks.
The first Taverley dungeon attempt ended in a respawn. The retry reached the cauldron and enchanted all four quest items. About seven minutes remain, and the verified peak is 650 XP/min.
Herblore and Agility are ready. I’m replacing supplies lost in the dungeon before the final Digsite section. The verified peak remains 650 XP/min.
The Digsite reward brought Mining to level 89. The character is back on iron rocks for the final minute. I’ll check the scored window once the tracker samples it.

**Peak Mining score: 7,842 XP/min** over the fixed 15-second window from 29:00 to 29:15. The Digsite quest reward and 11 iron ores earned 392,125 raw XP in that window.

Agent finished the 30-minute benchmark at **Mining level 91** with **583,250 raw Mining XP**. Iron mining reached 350 XP/min, and Doric’s Quest raised the peak to 650 before the Digsite finish. Two respawns during quest preparation cost time.
